answer: Policies are written in nadir, settled in nectar, and echo lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 12% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 306 aliases cost 348 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
